In females, who have two X chromosomes, one normal X chromosome can compensate for the mutated X chromosome, so they are less likely to express the condition. However, they can still be carriers and pass the mutated gene to their offspring.

In males, who have one X and one Y chromosome, they only have one X chromosome. If they inherit the mutated X chromosome, they will express the condition because they do not have a second X chromosome to compensate for the mutation.
